elements_not_encoded.text: First assess and manage airway, breathing, circulation and level of consciousness 16.
elements_not_encoded.reason: ABC assessment and pointer to 16; management.

elements_not_encoded.text: Identify all injuries and look for cause. Undress patient and assess front and back. If head or spine injury, use log-roll to turn. Then cover and keep warm.
Give sodium chloride 0.9% 1L IV hourly for 2 hours, then 500mL hourly. Aim for urine output > 200mL/hour. Stop if breathing worsens.
elements_not_encoded.reason: IV fluid for bruising with blood in urine.

elements_not_encoded.text: If shock1/SBP < 80, give sodium chloride 0.9% 1L IV rapidly, repeat until systolic BP > 80. Continue 1L 6 hourly. Stop if breathing worsens.
elements_not_encoded.reason: IV fluid if shock/SBP < 80; shock itself is encoded from footnote 1 as a probable diagnosis.

elements_not_encoded.text: If pain severe, give morphine 5-10mg IM or 3-5mg slow IV2. Avoid if severe head injury.
If poor perfusion, weakness/numbness below fracture, gently re-align into normal position.
If GCS < 15, neck/spine tenderness, weak/numb limb or abnormal pupils, apply rigid neck collar and sandbags/ blocks on either side of head.
elements_not_encoded.reason: Spinal immobilisation; its conditions (GCS < 15, neck/spine tenderness) are triggers for management only.

elements_not_encoded.text: If excessive or pulsatile bleeding, apply direct pressure and elevate limb.
If open fracture, remove foreign material, irrigate with sodium chloride 0.9% and cover with saline-soaked gauze. Discuss antibiotic management with referral ho
If pupils unequal or respond poorly to light, keep body straight and tilt to raise head (avoid bending spine).
If bleeding severe and persists, apply tourniquet above injury.
Splint limb to immobilise joint above and below fracture.
If pelvic fracture, tie sheet tightly around hips to immobilise.
Refer urgently. While awaiting transport, check BP, pulse, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation and GCS every 15 minutes.
elements_not_encoded.reason: Referral and 15-minute observations; vitals are routine.

elements_not_encoded.text: If open wound, suture as below and give tetanus toxoid 0.5mL IM if none in past 5 years.
If BP < 90/60, pulse > 100 or < 50, respiratory rate > 20 or < 9, oxygen saturation < 94% or drop in GCS, reassess airway, breathing, circulation, level of cons
elements_not_encoded.reason: Reassessment while awaiting transport in an already urgent patient (pointer to 16); not a new priority rule.

judgment_calls.decision: Footnote 1 list read as any-of (or), scoped to the injured patient (Traumatic injury, wound, fracture or head injury).
judgment_calls.alternatives: all-of (and); any2; leave unencoded; unscoped rule would fire on every tachycardic patient on any page.

judgment_calls.decision: Expanded to cold extremity, numbness of limbs and absent peripheral pulse; "pale" and the location "below" not representable.
judgment_calls.alternatives: Limb ischemia (narrower, warning sign uses Severe qualifier).

judgment_calls.decision: Finding of vomiting (count not representable), fires more often.
One check_for per red sub-box, chained: the injured-patient task (Traumatic injury) checks for wound, fracture, head injury, bruising and blood in urine; each of those triggers its own task.
judgment_calls.alternatives: One big task (would make wound/fracture/head injury self-referential with an or trigger).

judgment_calls.decision: Probable concussion = head injury and (mild headache or dizziness or mental fogginess), without negating the urgent criteria.
judgment_calls.alternatives: add (no ...) for every urgent head-injury sign.
